company.subscriptionOverride: You ticked {{slots}}, which is signed in by subscription right now. Saving writes an API key there, and that agent reads the key before the subscription — so the plan stops being used and billing moves to metered API usage. Untick it to keep the subscription.

shield.action: Take the keyboard and start typing in the terminal

status.preparing: Starting the sign-in command. The keyboard is on hold until you click the terminal, so early keystrokes cannot reach it as stray characters.
status.live: The terminal has your keyboard. Follow the prompts above.
status.succeededDetail: The process exited normally. Close this window; the account card will show the new state.
status.failedDetail: The process exited with code {{code}}. Read the terminal output above for the reason — a rejected login and a plan that does not cover this CLI both end here. You can run it again, or close and set an API key instead.
status.blocked: The terminal session could not start.
status.blockedUpdateGate: A source-update maintenance window is holding the writer lock, so no new terminal can start right now. Try again once it clears.
status.blockedForbidden: Your role may not run this command in a terminal. Ask an administrator, or close and set an API key instead.
status.blockedGeneric: The server refused to open this terminal.
status.blockedSharedLinkAdminOnly: On this shared server, linking Claude is limited to an owner or admin. Ask an owner or admin to link the account, or close and set your own API key instead.

claude.title: Two steps: authorize, then paste the code into the terminal
claude.intro: The terminal below runs <cmd>claude auth login</cmd>. It prints a sign-in link — open it in your own browser and authorize (no localhost required). This links your full Claude subscription, not an inference-only token.
claude.paste: After you authorize, the browser shows a code. Copy it and paste it back into this terminal at the Paste code here prompt, then press Enter. nassaj stores nothing itself — the Claude CLI saves the credential. When it finishes, the account card behind this dialog shows the new state.

codex.intro: The terminal below will display a link and a device code. Open the link in your browser and enter the code to authorize Codex — no localhost required.
codex.retry: Enable device code authorization for Codex in ChatGPT Security Settings, then run <cmd>codex login --device-auth</cmd> again.

kimi.intro: The terminal below runs <cmd>kimi login</cmd>, which prints a link and a device code. Open the link in your browser and enter the code to link your Kimi account — no localhost required.
kimi.subscription: This links a Kimi subscription. If you would rather use a metered API key, skip this and set the key in Settings → Vendors & credentials instead.

qwen.intro: Enter the Alibaba Cloud key issued for your Coding Plan or Token Plan. nassaj stores it encrypted for your account.
qwen.internationalHint: For most accounts outside mainland China
qwen.encrypted: Stored in the encrypted nassaj vault; never written to Qwen settings.
qwen.error: The credential could not be saved. Check the plan, region, and key, then try again.
qwen.successDescription: The encrypted credential will be used on the next Qwen message.

voiceTranscription.title: Accurate voice transcription
voiceTranscription.description: Turns your recording into text through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of the browser’s own speech recognition. Off by default, and inert without a key.
voiceTranscription.loadFailed: The transcription settings could not be read, so every control here is disabled. That does not mean the feature is off — its state is unknown.
voiceTranscription.stateOn: The microphone sends the recording to the endpoint set below and returns its text.
voiceTranscription.stateOff: The microphone stays on the browser’s recognition, and the transcription routes answer 404.

voiceTranscription.saveFailed: The setting could not be saved. The previous value still applies.

endpoint.hint: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works — Groq at https://api.groq.com/openai/v1, for example. https is required, except for a loopback address (127.0.0.1), which lets you point at an engine running on this machine.

voiceTranscription.languageNote: Choosing an engine is a language decision. A self-hosted Whisper on CPU transcribes English very well and Arabic poorly — for Arabic, a hosted endpoint is markedly more accurate.
